definitions.explanation: A wide field of view, most commonly used in photography and optics. Refers to lenses or camera settings that capture a broader scene than a standard lens.

examples.japanese: {広角|こうかく}レンズで{撮影|さつえい}した。
examples.english: I shot it with a wide-angle lens.

examples.japanese: {広角|こうかく}で{撮|と}ると{風景|ふうけい}が{広|ひろ}く{写|うつ}る。
examples.english: When you shoot wide-angle, the scenery appears broader.

examples.japanese: このスマートフォンのカメラには{広角|こうかく}モードが{搭載|とうさい}されている。
examples.english: This smartphone's camera has a wide-angle mode.

notes:
USAGE:
A compound of {広|こう} (wide, broad) + {角|かく} (angle). Almost exclusively used in photography and optics contexts. Most commonly appears in the compound {広角|こうかく}レンズ (wide-angle lens).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {広角|こうかく}レンズ (wide-angle lens)
- {広角|こうかく}モード (wide-angle mode)
- {超|ちょう}{広角|こうかく} (ultra-wide-angle)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {望遠|ぼうえん}: telephoto — the opposite end of the focal range, for distant subjects
- {標準|ひょうじゅん}: standard — a standard focal length, between wide-angle and telephoto
